step1_analysis.description: A passive LC resonator circuit including parasitic oxide capacitance and substrate resistance. It is used to model the core resonator of a VCO and its substrate noise coupling paths.

paper_reference.title: Performance Degradation of LC-Tank VCOs by Impact of Digital Switching Noise in Lightly Doped Substrates

resonant_frequency.description: The frequency at which the LC tank resonates (impedance phase crosses zero).

sky130_expected.calculation: f_res = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)) = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(1.2nH * 2.5pF))
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the reported L=1.2nH and C=2.5pF, the theoretical resonance is ~2.9 GHz. The paper's 3.5 GHz might imply a smaller effective capacitance in the actual VCO core.

quality_factor.description: The Q-factor of the tank, determined by the substrate parasitic losses and any inherent inductor resistance.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Without explicit inductor series resistance in the provided netlist, the Q is dominated by the substrate network (Cox and Rsub), leading to a relatively high Q in this isolated testbench.

peak_impedance.description: The maximum differential impedance of the tank at resonance.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the parasitic losses. With Q~100 and sqrt(L/C)~22 ohms, Z_max is in the low kOhm range.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the resonant frequency, peak impedance, and Q-factor of the LC tank by injecting an AC current and measuring the differential voltage.
